 //J U D G M E N T//

This claim petition is filed by the petitioners claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/- with interest from the date of petition till its realization for the death of Sri. Rajesh S/o.Venkatesh in a Road Traffic Accident.

2. The petition averments in brief is that:-
On 26.09.2021 at about 10.00 p.m., the deceased was proceeding on his motor cycle bearing Reg.No.52-R-0503 on Kunigal-Nelamangala NH-75 road, when he reached near, Suruchi Hotel, Maruru Hand Post, Kuduru, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time another motor Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
2 cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ER-2734 came from same direction with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life and dashed backside  SCCH-9 4 MVC.No.4113/2022 of deceased motor cycle.
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained head injury and other injuries all over the body.

He was shifted to Swasthya Hospital,
Nelamangala for treatment.
Wherein he succumbed to death while undergoing treatment at the Hospital.
Thereafter Post Mortem was conducted and the body was handed over to the petitioners.

The petitioners have spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards conveyance,
food and nourishment charges, transportation of dead body, funeral and obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and was Barber by profession and earning Rs.30,000/- p.m.

The petitioners have lost all his income and he was contributing his entire income to the family and he was only bread earner of their family and all the family members were depending upon on the income of the deceased for their livelihood.
The accident in question was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the  SCCH-9 5 MVC.No.4113/2022 rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ER-2734.

The Kuduru Police have registered a Criminal Case against the rider of the offending motor cycle in Cr.No.262/2021 Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
3 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279, 337 and 304 (A) of IPC.

sentences.text: After investigation the Police have filed Charge Sheet against the rider of offending motor cycle.
The respondents being Owner and Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners who lost their bread earner in the accident.
Hence, petitioners constrained to file a petition for compensation.
3. After service of notice the respondent No.1 remained absent and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 appeared through its counsel and filed its objection/written statement.

The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
 SCCH-9 6 MVC.No.4113/2022  This respondent has denied the contents of claim petition specifically and categorically.

It has denied the issuance of policy in respect of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ER-2734 and its validity and the policy has not been confirmed by the issuing office and the liability if any is strictly subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
It contended that the petition is bad for non joinder of proper and necessary parties i.e., owner and insurer of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-R-503 are the necessary parties.

It has specifically denies the occurrence, mode of accident and also involvement of Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
4 vehicle i.e., motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ER-2734 and petitioners have filed false case only with an intention to cause wrongful gain to this respondent and is put to strict proof of the same.

The respondent No.1 willfully entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident and it has clearly breached the terms and  SCCH-9 7 MVC.No.4113/2022 conditions of the policy and also violated Sec.149(2) of MV Act.
It has also denied the place, time and manner of accident.
It has also contended that there is no nexus between the alleged accident and the death of deceased.
It has also denied age, occupation and income of the deceased.
The alleged accident is only due to the sole negligence of the deceased himself.
The compensation claimed by the petitioners is highly excessive and exorbitant.
Hence, it has prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings my learned predecessor in office has framed the following issues;
 ISSUES  1. Whether petitioners prove that,
 deceased Sri.Rajesh S/o.Venkatesh  succumbed to the injuries sustained in RTA  on 26.09.2021 at about 10.00 p.m., while  the deceased was proceeding on his motor  cycle bearing Reg.No.KA-52-R-0503, when  reached near NH-75, Kunigal Nelamangala  Main Road, Suruchi Hotel, Maruru Hand  Post, Kudur, Magadi Taluk, Ramanagara  Dist., at that time the rider of the motor cycle  bearing Reg.No.KA-06-ER-2734 rode the  same recklessly without observing traffic  SCCH-9 8 MVC.No.4113/2022 Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
5  rules and dashed against the back side of  deceased motor cycle.

Due to the impact,
 deceased fell down and sustained grievous  injuries and succumbed fatal injuries on the  way to the Hospital?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled  for compensation?

If so, how much and from  whom?
 3. What order or award?
 5.
In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 herself examined as PW.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P1 to Ex.P11.
The respondent No.2/insurance company didn't choose to led its evidence.

6. I have heard the arguments of both side and perused the materials available on record;
 7.

My answer to the above issues are as under:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
 Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
Issue No.3:
Due to impact, deceased fell down and sustained head injury and other injuries all over the body and succumbed to death while he was undergoing treatment at the hospital.
9 . In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 examined as PW.1 and filed affidavit in lieu of chief examination by reiterating all the facts mentioned in the petition.
She also relied documents at Ex.P1 to P11.

The  SCCH-9 10 MVC.No.4113/2022 Ex.P1 is the FIR & Complaint, Ex.P2 is the Spot Mahazar, Ex.P3 is the Sketch, Ex.P4 is the Inquest Report, Ex.P5 is the Notice & Reply U/Sec.133 of M.V.Act, Ex.P6 is the Post Mortem Report, Ex.P7 is the IMV Report, Ex.P8 is the Charge Sheet, Ex.P9 is the Aadhaar card of petitioner, Ex.P10 is the Driving License of deceased and Ex.P11 is the copy of Ration Card.

10 . On perusal of these documents, it shows that the brother of deceased by name Vasanth Kumar had lodged First Information before Kudur Police Station,
alleging that on 26.09.2021, while he was in the house,
unknown public person had called him over phone and intimated that his brother had met with Road Traffic Accident.

He was also informed that at 7.45 to 8.00 p.m.,
Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
7

on Kunigal-Nelamangala Road, NH-75, near Marur Circle in front of Suruchi Hotel his brother was riding motor cycle bering No.KA-52-R-0503, at that time from Kunigal side a rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA-06-ER-2734  SCCH-9 11 MVC.No.4113/2022 rode in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to his brother's motor cycle.
Both the motor cycles were got damaged.
The riders of motor cycles were also sustained grievous injuries.
His brother one was shifted to Swasthya Hospital.
Hence he rushed into the hospital and learnt that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligence riding of vehicle bearing KA-06-ER-2734.
His brother died in the hospital while taking treatment.
Then he lodged the first information before concerned police.
On the basis of this first Information the Kuduru Police have registered the case in Cr.No.262/2021 for the offence punishable Under Sec.279, 337 & 304 (A) of IPC.

Thereafter, the Investigation Officer had conducted the Investigation and filed the Charge Sheet against the rider of the motor cycle by name Gangadhar for the offence punishable Under Sec.279 & 304(A) of IPC.

In the charge sheet also the charges leveled against rider of vehicle  SCCH-9 12 MVC.No.4113/2022 bearing No. KA-06-ER-2734 for the offences punishable U/sec 279 and 304A of IPC.
 11.

The respondent No.2 contended that the rider Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
8 of the offending motor cycle was not responsible for the cause of alleged accident.

sentences.text: The accident was caused only due to sole negligence of deceased.
Therefore the respondent No.2 is not liable to pay the compensation.
I have perused the materials available on record.
The charge sheet filed by investigating officer leveled charges of rash and negligent act of the rider of the offending motor cycle.

It is to be noted that though respondent No.2 contended that the rider of the offending motor cycle has not caused any accident and deceased was himself responsible for the cause of the alleged accident,
but showing of this aspect the respondent No.2 has not led any evidence.

As already stated above the Police records disclosing that the rider of the offending motor cycle has caused the accident by riding the vehicle in a  SCCH-9 13 MVC.No.4113/2022 rash and negligent manner and due to impact of this accident the deceased was sustained grievous injuries later succumbed to death while taking treatment in the hospital.
The Ex.P6/Post Mortem Report, discloses that death was caused due to "SHOCK AND HAEMORRHAGE AS A RESULT OF INJURIES SUSTAINED AND INJURY TO VITAL STRUCTURES SUCH AS BRAIN."
The death is not in dispute.

Further Ex.P3/rough hand Sketch prepared by Investigation Officer submitted along with charge sheet, discloses that the place of accident is Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
9 extreme left side of Kunigal-Nelamangala road.
In Ex.P3 the Police have pointed the place of accident and which is extremely on the left side of Kunigal-Nelamangala Road.
It substantiate the pleaidngs of petitioners.
The petitoneres contended that when deceased was proceeding towards Kunigal the rider of offending motor cycle dashed back side of deceased motor cycle.
The Ex.P3 also shows that the road is straight road and there
SCCH-9
14 MVC.No.4113/2022 is no turning or cross at the place of accident.
Further the Ex.P3 also shows that the road is 20 ft width road.
When the road is 20 feet width road, it is always open to the vehicles to overtake the other vehicle in the right side.

In the instant case, it appears that the rider of offending motor cycle, bearing No.KA-06-ER-2734 instead of taking right side directly hit the backside of the motor cycle of deceased who was moving extreme left side of the road.

Further the Ex.P7, which is the Motor Vehicle Accident Report also discloses that the motor cycle of deceased was damaged as under:
 1) Head light cover damaged  2) Front both side indicator's damaged  3) Crash guard damaged  4) Front left side foot rest damaged

The offending vehicle bearing No.KA-06-ER-2734 was also damaged as under:
 1) Front left side indicator damaged  2) Crash guard damaged  3) Head light assembly damaged  SCCH-9 15 MVC.No.4113/2022 Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
10
On perusal of these damages caused to the motor cycles, it discloses that almost front side of the parts of offending motor cycle were damaged.
Therefore, by considering all these aspects I am of the view that rider of offending motor cycle has caused the accident with rash and negligence riding of the motor cycle.
It is settled principles of law that the charge sheet is not a conclusive proof to fastened the negligence on the rider of the offending motor cycle.
It is the petitioner has to prove the negligence independently in a claim petition.
As stated above the Ex.P3 & Ex.P7 Sketch and IMV Report clearly shows that the negligence on the part of the rider of offending motor cycle not by the deceased.

12. That apart in a claim petition arising out of the accident the proving of negligence of offending vehicle is only preponderance of probabilities and not standard of proof beyond all reasonable doubt as required in criminal case.

This principles of law was laid down by the Hon'ble  SCCH-9 16 MVC.No.4113/2022 High Court of Karnataka, in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum & Others V/s Satbir &
others).

Under such circumstances, in the instant case,
there are sufficient materials to hold that the rider of offending motor cycle has caused the accident with rash and negligent manner and as a result deceased Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
11 sustained grievous injury and succumbed to death while undergoing treatment at hospital.
Further there is nothing on record to disbelieve the evidence of PW.1 with regard to cause of accident.

Under such circumstances,
it is held that the petitioners have proved the issue No.1
With this observations and discussion, I answered Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
13. Issue No.2:
In view of answering issue No.1 in the affirmative, the petitioners are entitled for compensation.

To assess the compensation, the Tribunal has to look into several factors like age, avocation,
income of deceased, conveyance charges, funeral and  SCCH-9 17 MVC.No.4113/2022 obsequies, towards loss of love and affection, etc., let me discuss one by one;
 (A) Towards Loss of dependency (loss of future earnings):
 i) In the petition the age of the deceased Rajesh is shown as 31 years.
The petitioners produced Ex.P9 - Aadhaar card of deceased, wherein the date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1990.
The date of accident is 26.09.2021, so the age of the deceased at the time of accident was 31 years.
The age mentioned in the Aadhaar card is taken into consideration as 31 years as on the date of accident.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
12

Supreme court of India in Smt. Sarla Verma case '16'
multiplier is applicable in present case.
ii) The PW.1 in her chief examination deposed that her husband was working as Barber and earning Rs.30,000/- per month.
In order to prove the income of  SCCH-9 18 MVC.No.4113/2022 deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.
In the absence of positive documents regarding deceased occupation and income this Tribunal will consider notional income.

iii) The Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, fixed notional income of the year 2021 at Rs. 15,000/- p.m.,
for determination of income before Lok-adalath for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Principal Benches, Bengaluru.

So in view of fixing of notional income by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, it is just and proper to this Tribunal to follow the notional income as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka to decide the cases before this Tribunal also.
The petitioners have not produced any relevant document to prove the income of deceased.

Accordingly,
the notional income of deceased during the year 2021 treated as Rs.15,000/- p.m., as fixed by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka.

Hence, this Tribunal has taken into  SCCH-9 19 MVC.No.4113/2022 consideration the income of deceased as Rs.15,000/-
per month.

13  iv)

In the case on hand, deceased was aged about 31 years.
Hence, in view of ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioners are entitled for additional 40% of salary to the future prospectus.
So, the total gross income of deceased is Rs. 21000/- per month  SCCH-9 20 MVC.No.4113/2022 (15,000 + 6000).
Admittedly deceased Rajesh was married, petitioner No.1 is wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 are children and petitioner No.4 & 5 are the parents of deceased
are considered as the legal heirs and dependents of the deceased.
So, petitioners are depending upon the income of deceased.

So, as per dictum of Hon'ble Supreme court in Smt.Sarla Verma case, where number of dependent family members is 4 to 6, 1/4th has to be deducted from the gross income of Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
14 deceased towards his personal expenses and remaining is to be taken as dependency.

Therefore, after deducting 1/4th from gross income it would comes at Rs.15,750/-
(21000-5250).
vi) Thus petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.30,24,000-00=(15,750x12xM16) as loss of dependency.
 SCCH-9 21 MVC.No.4113/2022  (B) Towards Consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses; In view of Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme court of India, in between United India Insurance Co. Ltd V/s Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur and others in Civil Appeal No.2705 of 2020 & National insurance company LTD V/s Pranay Sethi and Ors, the petitioner No.1 being the wife, petitioner No.2 & 3 being the minor children and petitioner No.4 & 5 being parents of deceased are entitled Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of spousal,

20. Regarding Liability:
The respondent No.2 contended that alleged accident was not caused by rider of offending vehicle and the accident was caused by the deceased himself.
As already stated above the respondent No.2 has not lead any evidence to prove his case.
Further this Court already held that the alleged accident was caused on the part of the negligence of the offending vehicle.
The respondent No.2 further contended that the rider of offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving license as on the date of accident.

Thus owner has violated the condition of policy and hence,
respondent No.2 not liable to the pay the compensation.

The charge sheet filed by the Investigation Officer against the rider of offending vehicle is not discloses any offences regarding not having valid driving license by the rider as  SCCH-9 23 MVC.No.4113/2022 on the date of accident.

Further in Ex.P.5 reply notice by the owner to Investigating Officer clearly stated that rider was having valid license, offending vehicle was insured and policy was valid from 31.8.2021 to 30.8.2022 as on the date of alleged accident.

Therefore, it shows that the Vedavathi vs Purushothama on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46570218/
16 rider of offending vehicle was possessing valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

sentences.text: The policy of insurance to the vehicle of respondent No.1 is also stated in the said Ex.P5.

Under such circumstances,
the respondent No.2 being a insurer is liable to pay the compensation.

Thus, it is already held that accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of offending vehicle, therefore, the respondent No.1 & 2 being Owner & Insurer of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.

However, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle is primarily liable to pay the compensation with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of  SCCH-9 24 MVC.No.4113/2022 petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative.
15 . Issue No.3:

For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/ s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,54,000/-(Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Four Thousand Only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners and respondent No.2 being insurer primarily liable to deposit the said compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
Out of the total compensation amount

, the petitioner No.1 being wife of deceased is entitled for 40%
and petitioner No.2 and 3 being minor children of deceased are entitled for 20% each and petitioner No.4 & 5 being parents of deceased is entitled for 10% each.

For the aforesaid reasons and discussion, the tribunal proceed to pass the following:
 ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioners U/ s.166 of Motor Vehicle Act is hereby partly allowed with cost.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.32,54,000/-(Rupees Thirty Two Lakhs Fifty Four Thousand Only) with interest at 6% p.a., from the date of petition till its realization.

, the petitioner No.1 being wife of deceased is entitled for 40%

17

In total amount apportioned to the share of petitioner No.2 and 3 an entire amount shall be deposited as FD in their names in the above bank till they attains the age of majority.
